summary: Prebuilt darwin-x64 binary implements PTY-over-WebSocket remote shell with ccfly C2 endpoints
details: The tarball ships a Mach-O Go binary at bin/ccfly-setup built from module path github.com/ccfly/rescue/cmd/setup. The binary links github.com/creack/pty and github.com/gorilla/websocket and contains hardcoded endpoints ws://ccfly, wss://, and https://cc.hn. The combination of a PTY allocator with a WebSocket client and hardcoded remote endpoints is the standard architecture of a remote-operator shell: the remote server writes into a PTY on the host and reads its output, giving full interactive shell access as the user that invoked the binary. The binary additionally contains the string ".zshrc" ("latest.zshrc.ccfly") alongside HTTP endpoints such as http://approveccfly-*/redeem, consistent with modification of the user's shell startup file to persist the agent across sessions. The package.json for this artifact declares no lifecycle scripts, no main, and no bin: it is a platform-specific (os=darwin, cpu=x64) payload delivered as an optionalDependency of a parent @ccfly/* wrapper, which is the component that invokes bin/ccfly-setup. When invoked, the binary opens a remote-controlled shell on the host and is capable of persisting via ~/.zshrc.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
